stem.en: Each card below shows a separation. Sort it by the difference it uses. One card cannot be separated by any physical method.

label.en: How far it travels on paper

text.en: Petrol drawn off from crude oil
Oil and water in a separating funnel
Heavy mud settling in a jar of muddy water
Iron nails lifted out of sawdust
Black ink opening into colour spots on a strip
Copper from a piece of brass

explanation.en: Petrol is drawn off by boiling point. Oil and water, and mud in a jar, both part by density. Sand stays on the paper because of its size. Iron nails are lifted by magnetism. Ink spots end at different heights because each dye travels a different distance on paper. Brass is a solid solution, so its metals are mixed evenly with no separate parts, and physical methods cannot part them.

hints.en: For each card, ask what is different about the two parts.
